implementerProof.how: Round five answers the third review round (changes requested at 315196597d1d: ci-filters red at the code head, and two minors). Since round four the branch carries 98f089a9 (the ci.yaml and docs-pages.yaml filters, and the two documents' existence-oracle sentence), two forward merges (46ce6085 and 525d94c5), and ba171533 (the claim-list check main's reflow broke). Both migrations are renumbered again: the Dispatch one to 0150_dpop_proofs after main took 0149, the broker one to 0021_oauth_pod_sessions after main took 0020. My workspace and the pod were recreated again, so the DPoP client was rebuilt from scratch — written once more from RFC 9449 and RFC 8693 with the Go standard library alone, never internal/broker/helper — and the whole battery re-driven at this head against a real broker and a real Dispatch with a counting proxy between them. Every one of the implementer's eight proofs holds, and the two minors were driven on the live surface rather than taken from their suites: the counting proxy was given a rewrite mode so an introspection answer the broker cannot be made to give — a named scope with an empty project, an unknown scope, an empty scope — reaches Dispatch's reader, and each is refused while the two answers the broker does write are accepted. Both migrations applied (the live Dispatch database reports version 150 with dpop_proofs; this run's broker database reports 21 with oauth_pod_sessions), and the CI-filter gate the review reported red passes here with 0 uncovered on each of its 28 gates.

None of the three was read as an unscoped caller, which is what the minor asked for. The person scope → 200 {"kind":"agent","owner":"ada@example.com","project":null,…} and, with the rewrite off, the broker's own named answer → 200 with project EXAMPLE.

observations: The refusal for an unusable project scope is the same 401 BROKER_TOKEN_NOT_A_SESSION, whose text says 'the secrets broker names no session for it', while the cause is the scope rather than a missing session. brokertoken.go:354-362 states that choice deliberately — one refusal for every answer the reader cannot take as a session's credential, telling a caller nothing of the broker's internals — so this is recorded as the behaviour it is, not as a defect. An operator reading only the message would look for the wrong thing; whether to narrow the wording is the reviewer's to weigh.
